chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Tha'laba, from Abdul Hamid ibn Awwad al-Taiy, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I have been upon him), 'I have taken a millstone, and my gathering place is in it, and my companions sit with me in it.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'That is the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.رَحًى: Millstone or mill, a tool for grinding grain, here used as a metonym for the place of work and gathering.
key_terms.مَجْلِسِي: My gathering place or sitting place.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling or virtue regarding using one's home or business as a gathering place for companions?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Abd al-Hamid ibn Awwad al-Ta'i reports to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) that he converted his mill into a gathering place for his companions. The Imam’s affirmation, describing this as 'rifq' (gentleness or ease) from Allah, underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on utilizing daily economic activities to foster communal bonds and religious learning. This highlights the integration of social welfare and spiritual community in Shia tradition, where convenience for the people is viewed as a divine mercy.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazaal, from Sa’alba, from Abdul Hameed Bin Awwaz Al Taiy who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I took a flour mill wherein was my gathering, and my companions tend to sit with me therein’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is a Mercy of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 26. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Tha’labah from ‘Abd al-Hamid ibn ‘ Awwad al-Ta’iy who has said the following: “I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that I owned a flour mill and that it had become my assembly place where my companions came together.
He (the Imam) said, ‘That is a blessing from Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.’”
